scope: Rehearsal lower thirds and ticker composition
Smooth scrolling in Preview and live outputs
Neutral idle cards with colored hover/active borders

fixes.change: Video and graphics share one canvas. Video is copied from the decoded-frame cache, with capture registered before source loading and released on cleanup. Animation uses RAF with a30fps fallback.
Both ticker paths reuse measured glyph strips; movement retains fractional positions. CanvasVerse paints existing buffers directly without React commits or canvas allocations per animation frame.
Double-click ensures the current pad is staged, then runs Show on Live. Second click does not toggle it away; edit remains separate.
One dialog contains selection, upload, preview, size, position and output targeting. Nested settings dialog and duplicate inner card heading removed.
Idle cards are neutral; hover uses the graphic color; staged/live cards keep matching colored borders and rings.

Stopped/missing/failed transports clear stale flags. Preview/Looks/Overview use actual transport status; pads also check whether the graphic is routed to that running output. Live chip is compact, explicitly labeled Live, and keeps full ticker text in its tooltip.

native.computerBackgroundControls: Opened rehearsal; exercised show/hide, start/stop, video pause and clear controls; staged ticker and sent it to hidden NDI; observed compact LIVE Scrolling text and off-air indicator after Stop.

rehearsal.method: Real component in actual native Tauri/WebKit, completely hidden nonfocusable window, six bounded settled pixel readbacks. All observations show decoded video painted and substantial lower-third/ticker pixels. Normal unmount and close completed.

limits: Foreground hover and native mouse double-click checks were not run under the no-interruption constraint. Automated double-click interaction tests pass.
OS window screenshots remained stale in the background; rehearsal composition was verified by native canvas readback instead.
A background-launched test window was reported over a fullscreen app; the isolated app was closed. All subsequent native checks used visible:false,focus:false,focusable:false windows.
